title: World 1 purchase-value upgrade proposal and complete retained-family crosswalk
current_owner_direction: 10 worlds, 50 levels each; World 1 art focus
Meaningful appearance changes must accompany useful input/output/work/defense/attack value
Multiple pets and survivors may be active simultaneously

supersession.older_briefs: W1UP-01 through W1UP-15 are low-impact initial studies, superseded as the active generation direction. Their files and generated iterations remain history, not final owner-selected art.
rules_replaced: Do not invent any pet/survivor appearance progression is superseded by explicit owner request for their gear/training/attack/work progression.
All new tier footprints and ports fixed is superseded: later purchased stages may expand with explicit route, clearance and migration contracts.
Storehouse needs no new work because three static forms exist is superseded: storage now receives its own substantial functional progression.
rules_retained: Keep selected conveyor and resource unit scale
Do not equate 50 world levels with 50 equipment appearances
Do not claim concept art proves native behavior or balanced benefits

purchase_value_requirements: A baseline limitation the player actually experiences
A distinct useful operation, choice or protection/attack improvement
A visible structure/mechanism/tool/gear change that explains it
Actual conserved input-to-operation-to-output or job/target path
Declared purchased footprint, ports, route and blocked-state behavior
Reachable requirements and meaningful cost/maintenance/supply/space tradeoffs
No resale of an ability already granted by baseline
Measured numeric gain and affordability before gameplay approval

shared_preserved_baselines.survivor_carry: Unlimited logical mixed raw, processed and ordinary cash remains baseline. Gear must not sell capacity.
shared_preserved_baselines.survivor_jobs: Eligible trained/equipped survivors already have full human-task parity, delegated budgeted purchases, hunting and authorized attacks; improvements may increase measured efficiency/protection/coordination without arbitrarily removing baseline competence.
shared_preserved_baselines.pets: All seven already attack and have registered useful specialties; upgrades improve existing attack/work performance, protection and tactics.
shared_preserved_baselines.storage: Typed organization, material/food/hide/timber/fuel bays and central access already exist. New value is workflow, simultaneous access, staging, protected handling and any actually implemented bounded storage increase.
shared_preserved_baselines.mortality: Pets/survivors can die; ordinary paid replacement preserves earned companion XP/skills. Estate custody is separate. New gear must not create free revival or clone estate stock.
shared_preserved_baselines.counter: Bulk self-service goods and separate cash, no register/cashier or spawned attendant.
shared_preserved_baselines.furnace: 10 existing source appearances retained; blackout and paid level-1 rebuild stay binding.
shared_preserved_baselines.resource_conservation: New parallel machines consume separate inputs and produce separately committed outputs. More heads do not multiply the same input.
shared_preserved_baselines.vehicle: Low fuel required, four wheels/two axles and low horizontal blades retained. VC01/VC02 remain unresolved; no direct warehouse truck unloading is added.
shared_preserved_baselines.pet_world_availability: All-seven-species planning retains each source world/region availability. It does not unlock all seven in World 1; illustrative teams require their actual eligibility.

team_policy.latest_owner_requirement: Multiple pets and survivors can be active simultaneously.
team_policy.prior_staged_policy: WHOLE_GAME_COMPLETENESS.json CD04 proposes up to three expedition pets and two survivor escorts; separately assigned local survivors and useful reserve-pet jobs are not that escort cap.
team_policy.status: Prior staged policy retained for review; not newly ratified, not claimed integrated or measured. No new total-population cap or paid active slot is authored.

proposed_ammunition_contract.recipe: Existing planks plus existing mechanical_parts become simple wooden-shaft metal-head bolts at an attainable workshop/manual crafting station. Exact recipe quantities, output count and cost remain tuning decisions.
reachable_chain: planks + mechanical_parts -> proposed workshop bolt recipe
proposed_ammunition_contract.gate: Define real item/recipe/projectile IDs, affordability and manual bootstrap route before ballista runtime adoption. No ammunition may appear for free; no new gunpowder or electricity chain is assumed.

numeric_policy.rate_capacity_HP_damage_price_values: Not frozen by this package; any future numeric values must be visibly labeled tuning proposals and measured on an achievable free-player route.
numeric_policy.hardware_counts: Visible proposed hardware counts, such as two saw cells or four/six wheat heads, describe authored geometry only and do not assert rate multipliers or unlock levels.

ladders.name: Saw station / authored sawmill progression
ladders.retained_base: Selected hand-cranked timber saw station remains the historical base; uninspected lumber_mill/steam_saw archive images are not used as visual evidence.

stages.name: FEED MILL
stages.baseline_limitation: One small worktable requires repeated loading, clamping and loose plank collection.
stages.appearance_change: Long timber-and-blue mill bed, elevated raw-log cradle and metering gate, captive moving clamp, guarded circular cutting head, long plank outfeed and a finished-stack cradle. One reachable manual crank drives the cutter and mechanically linked feed rollers.
stages.purchase_value: A real buffered feed-and-cut cycle reduces repeated handling stops and presents one reachable output pickup point. The exact measured gain is pending.
stages.input_processing_output: Existing wood enters at the mill left end, waits in a raw cradle, moves through one clamped cutting head and leaves as existing planks at the right end. No new product or changed recipe yield.
stages.jobs: Bulk supply at the left cradle; operate/clear at the front controls; collect the right finished stack without crossing the cutting path.
stages.footprint_ports_clearance: A purchased longitudinal extension beyond the base table. Left raw receiving, right plank discharge, front continuous worker service lane; rear mechanical access remains clear.
stages.tradeoff: Requires a larger plot and paid construction; it can starve if wood is not supplied or stop if the finished cradle is blocked.
requirements: Existing wood-to-planks recipe and conserved typed buffers
Reachable existing wood/planks/metal component construction chain with a raw bootstrap bill if needed
Visible feed/contact/cut/output/blocked/damage states
One real manual-crank workstation with linked roller/cutter operation; idle without an assigned living operator. No new power or fuel commodity.

stages.name: PARALLEL SAWMILL
stages.baseline_limitation: A single cutting cell remains the bottleneck while harvesting and orders grow.
stages.appearance_change: A broad twin-bay timber mill frame with two parallel log-feed beds and two distinct guarded saw heads, a shared raised receiving rack, independent fixed finished-plank collection cradles and a partial snow canopy. No stacking arm or gantry.
stages.purchase_value: Two independently reserved cutting jobs can run concurrently and dispatch separately; one blocked outfeed need not stop the other. This is proposed concurrency, not an automatic double-yield claim.
stages.input_processing_output: Two left-side raw cradles feed two parallel cutting beds; two right-side plank cradles remain distinct. Each job consumes its own real wood and commits only its own planks.
stages.jobs: Two independently staffed manual-crank workstations operate separate cutting cells: the front cell crank faces the front service walk; the rear cell crank faces the rear service walk. Reach the rear walk by an exterior end bypass outside the cutting and material-transfer aprons. No crossing between blades.
stages.footprint_ports_clearance: Wider purchased mill yard with separate outward front and rear service walks, fixed left receiving and right dispatch aprons, and an exterior end bypass outside all blade/feed/output sweeps. Each independent crank is reachable from its own outward walk; neither operator crosses another lane.
stages.tradeoff: Larger bill, greater wood demand and higher repair burden; useful concurrency requires supply and clear destinations. No free output while a lane is empty.
requirements: Independent cell reservations and per-job input/output receipts
Mass balance and blocked-output backpressure per lane
Multiple living-worker assignments with shared destination reservations
Expanded collision footprint, pathfinding and belt-port layout preview before purchase
Each cell is manually driven by its own assigned eligible living operator; an unstaffed cell remains idle. A blocked/full output holds only its affected lane.
Both stages use fixed independent output collection cradles; no stacking arm, gantry, hoist or unbound loading actuator is included.
